title: MV Sending Captured Monsters to Storage (DreamX_CaptureEnemies)

posts.author: KayronDEV
posts.body:
Hi everyone! I’m working on a monster-catching game in RPG Maker MV, and I’m running into an issue combining two plugins via an event:
[DreamX_CaptureEnemies.js]
Allows capturing enemies and converting them into party members using <capture_actor_id:x> notetag.
[MonsterStorageBox.js]
Adds a PC-style monster storage box where you can deposit and withdraw actors.
They actually work fine, DreamXs plugin creates copies of actors and I can deposit and withdraw those copies without trouble. What I want is when I capture a monster during battle, I want the game to check if the party already has 6 members (which is the maximum) and if it's full, send the next captured monster to the storage box. This is exactly what games like Pokemon do when you reach maximum capacity in your party.
DreamXs plugin has the notetag <capturedSwitch:x> ( with x as the switch ID as an enemy notetag to set the switch to true when the enemy is captured) so I think I can use this in an event, but I think that is too complicated, and I don't even know how to start this event.
Can someone help me with this? That's a core mechanic in my game!
Thank you in advance for your help!
Let me know if you need screenshots or a demo.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Edit:
The
$gameParty.members()
method only returns the number of Party members in battle, only 4, only on the map it returns the total, so the best option would be to use
$gameParty._actors
which returns an Array with the IDs directly.
I also wouldn't use IF inside the Script command, as this would prevent the dev from including other event commands, such as a simple warning message.
Another thing, let's say that by chance you decide to have the option of capturing two or more monsters in the same battle, then in this case you will need to use a cycle (repeat until completed):
Code:
◆Loop
  ◆If：Script：$gameParty._actors.length > 6
    ◆Script：let actor = $gameParty._actors[6];
    ：      ：alert(actor);
    ：      ：$gameSystem.depositedActors.push(actor);
    ：      ：$gameParty.removeActor(actor);
    ◆Text：None, None, Dim, Top
    ：    ：Este monstro foi enviado para o depósito...
    ◆
  ：Else
    ◆Break Loop
    ◆
  ：End
  ◆
：Repeat Above
It is not possible to capture all the event fields, so I put the code directly

I just tested the script that you proposed, both of them. The enemy is captured and send to the party and no text is shown. So, it didn't work.
I checked a AI code assistant to tell me how DreamX plugin capture system works, I hope that it can help:
DreamX_CaptureEnemies uses two ways to add captured monsters:
Sometimes it adds during the battle ($gameParty.addActor(newId)).
Sometimes only after the battle (BattleManager._capturedEnemies → added in updateBattleEnd).
I don't know, but maybe Before adding the monster (or immediately after), we need to calculate how many actors were there before. If the party already had 6 members before adding, the capture should go straight to storage.

Feels like the code works, the issue is with the timing. It seems the in battle timing isn't working well; you could try changing the Span to "Moment" instead of Turn, with Conditions of "Turn 0 + 1*X". That's a bit risky, because it will try to run constantly, and could slow your game down; so you'd want to add a "Wait 2" command somewhere in the loop to give your game a little chance to breathe.

Yeah, was afraid of that. If running it in the battle isn't working, you can try a plugin that will run a common event after every battle ends, and put the code into that common event. For example, SumRndmDde's Battle End Events plugin:
http://sumrndm.site/battle-end-events/
Set each parameter to the same common event, then in that common event run the code to check if the party is too large. This would mean you can have 7 members whilst still in the battle, but it should get rid of the extra one to the deposit box as soon as the battle ends.
